text:
Maya P: Quick sync — customer ops asked for a clear upgrade handoff for on-prem bundles + customer-managed networking. Need checklist and launch bar.
Alex W: +1. Are we aligning on zero-downtime or a short maintenance window? Customers vary.
Ryan C: Customer asked specifically for automated BGP handshake + egress NAT preservation during upgrade. They can't re-IP nodes.
Sam R: Priority: 1) safe upgrade choreography 2) verifiable offline bundles 3) documented networking contract. Can we draft minimal acceptance criteria?
Tariq S: Proposal: support two upgrade modes — rolling (zero-downtime for stateless runtime) and fenced (short maintenance for control-plane migrations). Rolling requires stable KV migration and in-place KV v2 compatibility.
Maya P: Ok. For launch gate I want: a) upgrade tests with real customer topologies b) preflight network verification c) rollback plan && tooling to rebind IPs.
Alex W: For customer-managed networking we should publish an explicit "handshake contract" without implying we touch their routers. e.g., expected BGP routes, allowed ASNs, MTU, and required firewall rules.
Ryan C: Also include a small lightweight connectivity-check tool that runs from the agent and produces a JSON report the customer can paste in support cases.
Sam R: Acceptance criteria draft (short): [must pass in lab with 95th%-ile path], [installer hash verified], [preflight verifying egress routes and NAT retention], [upgrade completes within SLA or clearly documents downtime].
Maya P: Can someone write a sample preflight output so we know the data shape? Keep it human-readable and machine-parseable.
Tariq S: I put a tiny example in the thread:
```
preflight: {
  agent_version: "2.4.0",
  network_checks: ["bgp-peer:reachable","egress-ip-stable","dns-resolve"],
  issues: ["egress-ip-changed"]
}
```
Alex W: We'll need to standardize keys — use snake_case and a schema version header: preflight_v1. That avoids compatibility surprises.
Ryan C: Field test note: a customer with NAT-preserving on upgrade will still have ephemeral pod IP changes. We must document that service-led affinity won't survive unless they use sticky load-balancers.
Sam R: Ok next steps: 1) eng-runtime — draft rolling/fenced choreography and failure modes 2) devex — cli preflight tool + sample report 3) docs — handshake contract and upgrade runbook 4) cs — pick 2 pilot customers (one small, one complex) for validation.
Maya P: Timeline? Want a rough 6-week pilot prep — not shipping yet, just ready to validate with pilots.
Alex W: Sounds doable. I'll sketch the choreography this week. Will include sequence numbers and idempotency notes for agent bootstrap.
Tariq S: Also flag: offline package verification for air-gapped installs. We need checksum + sig verification and an offline-only preflight mode.
Ryan C: Could we include a minimal example of the agent config that preserves customer egress? Something like:
```
network:
  egress_mode: preserve_ip
  bgp:
    enabled: true
    asn: 65012
    neighbors: ["10.0.0.1"]
```
Sam R: Nice. Devex can bake that into `redwood-check preflight --format=json`.
Maya P: Ops-bot will post build status for the preflight tool when it's ready.
ops-bot: build/redwood-check preflight v0.1 triggered by @Tariq S — CI queued :gear:
Alex W: I'll add a section on rollback triggers: if KV migration lag > 30s or bgp-neighbor loss then abort and roll back leader change.
Ryan C: One more ask from field: a customer wants a network dry-run mode where we simulate route changes without advertising them. Can be heavy but valuable for complex infra.
Tariq S: We can support a dry-run that outputs the BGP announcements that would be made and a validation pass against the preflight model.
Sam R: I'll create a short PRD with those acceptance criteria and link pilot tickets. Target to share with the team by Friday.
Maya P: Great. Tagging @Ryan C and @Alex W for engineering follow-up. I'll schedule a 30m sync after PRD is up. :calendar:
Alex W: Thanks — will follow up with a choreography diagram and explicit step numbers.
